newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dow offers to buy S.Africa Sentrachem.
newsitem.headline: Dow offers to buy S.Africa Sentrachem.

text.p: United States chemical giant Dow Chemical Co said on Monday it had offered to buy South African-based chemical firm Sentrachem Ltd for a price of 10.50 a share.
The bid values Sentrachem at 2.074 billion rand.

Sentrachem, with annual sales of 5.5 billion rand, has its main businesses in speciality chemicals and agricultural chemicals. It also operates in polypropylene, polyethylene, latex, rubber and chlor-alaki products.
Dow said it had already sealed an agreement from Sankorp Ltd, which holds 38.74 percent of Sentrachem, to accept and recommend the offer.
"We have agreed to accept Dow's offer and make the same positive recommendation to the minority shareholders of Sentrachem," said Sankorp executive director and Sentrachem chairman Attie du Plessis.
Dow first entered the South African market in 1959 but pulled out during the 1980s as firms faced pressure to disinvest from the former white-ruled state.

However, the firm returned to South Africa after an eight year absence in 1995, a year after the country's first fully democratic elections, to operate a polyurethane plant near Durban on the Indian Ocean coast.

"This acquisition reinforces our strategic direction to enhance Dow's performance-chemicals portfolio with the addition of Sentrachem's strong speciality and agricultural chemicals businesses, among others," said William Stavropoulos, Dow chief executive and president.
Dow is the world's fifth largest chemicals company with annual sales of more than $20 billion, about 40,000 employees and customers in 157 countries.
Earlier the Johannesburg Stock Exchange suspended Sentrachem's shares pending an announcement.

Sentrachem embarked on a huge restructuring on June 24 aiming to net greater focus and efficiency. The restructure proposed the merger of its NCP and Karbochem units and plans to cut costs by 300-350 million rand at its Sanachem unit.

Sentrachem had a disastrous half year to end February in which one-off charges of 261 million rand due to forward cover contracts and restructuring costs at unit Sanachem plunged the group into a pre-tax loss of 257 million rand.
